newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers get optimistic on US debt - MCM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers get optimistic on US debt - MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers were more sanguine about U.S. debt markets last week and extended durations slightly on their portfolios, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.
"This investor group used weakness last week to extend durations slightly," said MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague, who conducts the asset allocation survey.
"They're still bullish, and are seeking ways to take advantage of bullish fundamentals," he said.
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark slipped to 108.1 percent in the week ended December 16 from 107.9 percent in the prior week.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 22 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," up from 21 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" fell to 21 percent, down from 32 percent in the week ended December 9.
Fifty-seven percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, up from 47 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets fell to 2.16 percent, against 2.35 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 29 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, up from 27 percent the previous week, while 12 percent underweighted it. The remaining 59 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 41 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 11 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 40 domestic participants, who manage about $100 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
